messages:
Aisha: FYI - competitor pushed a homepage update for 'QuickServe Edge' claiming "'lower unit cost and enterprise routing parity'". We need a quick decision: ship launch focusing on our differentiators or push hard on parity messaging? Any immediate thoughts?

Diego: Don't mirror their claim. We should map customer asks -> launch lanes. Two lanes make sense: 1) Core differentiated launch (public) 2) Controlled compatibility lane (private/pilot).

Priya: From an eng perspective, full parity (runtime behavior + controls) is nontrivial. We can do a limited compatibility layer for Dedicated tenants to satisfy pilots, but it needs feature flags, telemetry, and a rollback plan.

Tom: Sales: two pilot customers asked specifically for tenant-level routing controls this morning. If we can offer a paid pilot (3mo) with a compatibility wrapper, we secure renewals. They accept limitations if documented.

Jess (marketing): For public-facing copy I recommend avoiding any numeric cost comparisons. Use benefit-led lines like "optimized inference economics" and "enterprise-grade routing controls" without implying identical metrics. Legal will want soft language. :memo:

legal-bot: Reminder: do not publish comparative claims about competitor performance without documented, reproducible benchmarks and prior legal review.

Aisha: Proposed public positioning bullets:
- "Predictable latency and transparent unit economics"
- "Unified control across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments"
- Avoid direct competitor naming or percentage claims.

Priya: Tech plan for compatibility lane (high level):
- Spike to validate adapter approach (token passthrough + header mapping) - 10d
- Runtime flag per-tenant: compat_enabled:true
- Telemetry: compat_fallbacks, latency_delta_ms
- Auto-disable if p95 > SLA + 100ms for 5m
Sample flag object: 
```
compat_enabled: true
compat_profile: "routing-v1"
telemetry: ["compat_fallbacks","latency_delta_ms"]
```

Diego: Launch criteria (both lanes):
- Perf: p50/p95 within target envelope on canonical workloads
- Quality: no regression on eval prompt set
- Documentation: migration guide + limitations page
- Legal: copy approved

Tom: Pricing note for the pilot: bill as professional services + premium support. Will present draft SOW to pilot customers.

Jess (marketing): I'll prepare hero variants and a one-sheet that highlights predictable economics + reliability. Keep hero generic: "Predictable inference for production apps".

Aisha: Action items:
- Priya: spike + risk doc for adapter (due 2463001170)
- Diego: finalize lane definitions & launch checklist (due 2463001190)
- Jess: hero + one-sheet drafts for legal review (due 2463001200)
- Tom: pilot SOW draft and customer list (due 2463001220)

Priya: Adding note: if we open compatibility lane, require customer acceptance of known limitations (edge cases list). saves eng cycles.

Diego: Agreed. We'll save any aggressive parity claims for internal sales collateral only. public messaging stays differentiated. :thumbsup:

Aisha: Thanks team. We'll regroup after the spike results. If anything else pops up, ping here.

legal-bot: Legal review requested (ticket LR-4821). Please attach marketing drafts.

Tom: pinging pilot prospects. thanks! :rocket:
